$comment: Ratchet baselines. Each entry is a violation count that is allowed to shrink and never to grow.
GATE-TOPOLOGY.md §2.3a: these instruments have never run on this repository, so their first run
produces findings in the hundreds. Paying them down as a precondition would stall issue #2 behind
unrelated work; running them non-blocking would make them annotation, which is level 5 with a
config file on. So they block on INCREASE from the day they land.
An unknown key is a failure, not a pass. A linter that appears in a run but not here means the
enabled set moved without the baseline moving with it, and the gate must not treat that as zero.
When a count drops, commit the lower number in the same PR that dropped it. A baseline left above
the truth is headroom for a regression nobody will see.

platform_note: Pinned to the enforcing platform, which is the CI runner, because the analysed file set is a
function of the build tags in force. gcc is present on the runner and absent on a bare Windows
host, so `//go:build cgo` selects oracle_cgo.go and open_cgo.go there and their `!cgo` twins
here. Measured 2026-08-08: errcheck 30 on linux/cgo=1, 28 on windows/cgo=0, every other linter
A run on another platform still blocks on an increase -- an increase is real everywhere -- but
the lane refuses to call its lower numbers a shrink. Fewer findings because fewer files

measured_note: 6 findings over 909 Go files in cmd/, internal/ and tests/, after the scanner itself was
fixed: substring matching and a guessed exemption list had produced 483, of which 1 was real.
The 6 are 3 production sites (lifecycle.go:17 names shopee in the integrations domain, twice
on one line; ingest_service.go:334 and assisted_sankhya_linkage_service.go:296 both branch on
"mercado_livre" in the application layer) and 2 test call sites discarding the bool from
.Value(). All are real debt: vendor identity as control flow outside the vendor-aware layers,
and unknown-reads-as-zero. Ratcheted rather than paid because the fixes change production
behavior and an instrument PR must not.
26 findings over 220 tracked .ts/.tsx sources, 0 parse failures. §2.3a predicted hundreds; it
was wrong in the cheap direction, and the number is small enough that paying it down is a real
option rather than a stall. It is still landed as a ratchet, because the rules have to block on
increase from the day they exist -- a debt of 26 that grows is worse than one that does not.
Unlike golangci-lint this count is not platform-dependent: there are no build tags in
TypeScript, the file set comes from `git ls-files`, and the .ts/.tsx line endings are pinned to
LF in .gitattributes. The lane's coverage assertion is the real guard -- every tracked source
must appear in the report, because a file outside tsconfig.eslint.json is reported as clean by
the three type-aware rules that could not run on it.
